name: brand_analytics_get_search_term_momentum
description:
Returns weekly search term momentum data from Brand Analytics search query performance: your click share, WoW delta, 4-week and 12-week rolling averages, top-3 competitor ASINs with click/conversion shares, and a computed momentum signal.

Use this tool to:
- Track how your click share on a search term is trending (accelerating, growing, stable, declining, collapsing)
- Identify search terms where you are losing or gaining momentum vs competitors
- See which competitor ASINs hold the top 3 positions and their conversion shares
- Find weak leader opportunities where rank-1 has low conversion share
- Spot defensive priorities where competitors are gaining share on your keywords

IMPORTANT: Results are capped by the 'limit' parameter (default 100). When search_terms is omitted, ALL search terms are considered but only the top N by sort order are returned. A company may have thousands of tracked search terms. To explore different keyword groups: (1) change sort field/direction to surface different terms, (2) use search_terms filter with match_type='contains' to drill into a keyword theme (e.g., ['ring'] returns all ring-related terms), or (3) use brand/product_family filters to narrow by product line.

Portfolio aggregation: By default this tool returns detail rows at search term × ASIN × marketplace grain. To get portfolio-level keyword momentum, set query.aggregation.group_by, for example ['search_term', 'marketplace']. In grouped mode, search_volume is de-duplicated with MAX instead of summed across ASIN rows, and momentum fields are recomputed from weekly portfolio click share.

Momentum signals explained:
- accelerating: WoW up AND 4-week avg above 12-week avg (sustained upward trend)
- growing: WoW up (recent positive movement)
- stable: no significant WoW change
- declining: WoW down (recent negative movement)
- collapsing: WoW down AND 4-week avg below 12-week avg (sustained downward trend)
- new: first appearance (no prior week data)

Integration note: Use with brand_analytics_get_keyword_funnel_metrics to understand the full funnel behind a search term, or with brand_analytics_get_competitive_landscape for raw report-level detail.

Knowledge base: https://help.neonpanel.com/en/articles/brand-analytics-competitive

query.description: Shared query envelope for Brand Analytics tools.

company_ids.description: Company identifier(s) - required for multi-tenant isolation.

search_terms.description: Optional: filter by specific search terms. When omitted, ALL search terms are included (subject to 'limit'). Use with match_type='contains' to explore keyword themes (e.g., ['ring'] returns all ring-related terms). Combine multiple terms: ['ring', 'bracelet'].

intent_ids.description: Optional: filter to search terms mapped to any of these intent_ids. AND-combined with `search_terms`. Get available intent_ids from brand_analytics_list_user_intent_clusters.

asins.description: Optional: filter to rows where your ASIN matches.

competitor_asins.description: Optional: filter to search terms where these ASINs appear in top 3.

marketplaces.description: Amazon marketplace code(s) (e.g., 'US', 'UK', 'DE'). Multiple markets supported.

revenue_abcd_class.description: Optional: filter by revenue classification (A=top revenue, D=lowest). Source: etl.asin_revenue_class_daily, rebuilt every day at 07:00 UTC; see the classification_as_of field for the date it was computed on.

pareto_abc_class.description: Optional: filter by Pareto ABC classification (A=top 80% revenue, B=next 15%, C=bottom 5%). Source: etl.asin_revenue_class_daily, rebuilt every day at 07:00 UTC; see the classification_as_of field for the date it was computed on.

product_family.description: Optional: filter by product family name(s). Narrows to search terms associated with specific product families.

momentum_signal.description: Optional: filter by computed momentum signal. Values: accelerating (WoW up + 4w > 12w), growing (WoW up), stable, declining (WoW down), collapsing (WoW down + 4w < 12w), new (first week).

group_by.description:
Optional dimensions for grouped/portfolio output (max 3). Empty or omitted returns detail rows per search term × ASIN × marketplace. Use ['search_term', 'marketplace'] for one portfolio row per keyword per marketplace, or ['intent'] for portfolio momentum bucketed by primary intent. In grouped mode, search_volume is de-duplicated and click-share trend metrics are recomputed from weekly portfolio share.

Output columns by dimension:
- 'intent' → intent_id, primary_intent_label
- 'search_term' → search_term
- 'marketplace' → marketplace
- 'company' → company_id
- 'brand' → my_brand
- 'product_family' → product_family
- 'asin' → asin

periods_back.description: Number of weeks to look back from most recent data.

field.description: Column to sort by. A 'rank' column (1-based) is added to the output reflecting this sort order. Use wow_delta DESC to find biggest gainers, wow_delta ASC for biggest losers.

direction.description: Sort direction. DESC for highest-first (top performers, biggest opportunities). ASC for lowest-first (biggest decliners, weakest positions).

select_fields.description: Optional output field selection. When provided, only these fields are returned per row — reduces response size. If omitted, returns all columns. IMPORTANT: Use exact field names from the enum.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return (default 100, max 200). Only the top N rows by the chosen sort order are returned. Use filters to focus on specific keyword segments.

match_type.description: Keyword matching strategy for search_terms filter.

weak_leader_detection.description: Configure what defines a 'Weak Leader' opportunity.

max_leader_conversion_share.description: Leader is 'weak' if conversion share below this threshold (default 15%).

min_search_volume.description: Only flag weak leaders on keywords with search volume at or above this.

min_click_share.description: Only return terms where my_click_share >= this value.

min_search_volume.description: Only return terms with search volume >= this value.

rank.description: 1-based row number reflecting the chosen sort order.

search_term.description: The search query shoppers typed on Amazon.

company_name.description: Company name associated with this data row.

company_id.description: Company id when grouped by company.

company_count.description: Number of companies represented in a grouped row.

marketplace_count.description: Number of marketplaces represented in a grouped row.

search_volume.description: Relative search volume for this term (higher = more popular).

period_start.description: Start date of the reporting week.

period_end.description: End date of the reporting week.

my_asin.description: Your ASIN that appears in top-3 clicked for this search term.

my_brand.description: Your brand name associated with my_asin.

my_click_share.description: Detail mode: your ASIN's click share for this term. Grouped mode: portfolio click share for the grouped row, capped at 1.0.

portfolio_click_share.description: Grouped mode only: summed portfolio click share across distinct ASIN rows for the grouped week, capped at 1.0.

portfolio_click_share_uncapped.description: Grouped mode only: raw summed portfolio click share before the 1.0 cap. Use this to spot overlapping or duplicated ASIN share rows.

prev_week_share.description: Your click share from the previous week (0-1 scale).

wow_delta.description: Week-over-week change in click share (this week minus last week). Positive = gaining share.

avg_share_l4w.description: Average click share over the last 4 weeks (0-1 scale). Smooths out weekly noise.

avg_share_l12w.description: Average click share over the last 12 weeks (0-1 scale). Shows long-term trend.

momentum_signal.description: Computed momentum classification: 'accelerating' (WoW up + 4w > 12w), 'growing' (WoW up), 'stable', 'declining' (WoW down), 'collapsing' (WoW down + 4w < 12w), 'new' (first week).

revenue_abcd_class.description: Revenue ABCD class of the ASIN (A=highest revenue, D=lowest). Source: etl.asin_revenue_class_daily, rebuilt every day at 07:00 UTC; see the classification_as_of field for the date it was computed on.

pareto_abc_class.description: Pareto ABC class (A=top 80% revenue, C=long tail). Source: etl.asin_revenue_class_daily, rebuilt every day at 07:00 UTC; see the classification_as_of field for the date it was computed on.

product_family.description: Product family grouping from ASIN attributes.

revenue_share.description: Revenue share of this ASIN within its company portfolio (0-1 scale). Higher = more important product.

total_revenue_share.description: Grouped mode only: summed revenue share across ASIN rows represented in the group.

avg_asin_click_share.description: Grouped mode only: average ASIN click share inside the grouped row.

max_asin_click_share.description: Grouped mode only: strongest single-ASIN click share inside the grouped row.

asin_count.description: Grouped mode only: number of distinct ASINs represented in the grouped row.

portfolio_asins.description: Grouped mode only: comma-separated sample of up to 25 ASINs represented in the grouped row.

top_asin_by_click_share.description: Grouped mode only: ASIN with the highest click share in the grouped row.

rank_1_asin.description: ASIN with the highest click share (position #1).

rank_1_clickshare.description: Click share of the #1 ASIN (0-1 scale).

rank_1_conversionshare.description: Conversion share of the #1 ASIN (0-1 scale). Low conversion + high clicks = weak leader.

rank_2_asin.description: ASIN with the 2nd highest click share.

rank_2_clickshare.description: Click share of the #2 ASIN (0-1 scale).

rank_2_conversionshare.description: Conversion share of the #2 ASIN (0-1 scale).

rank_3_asin.description: ASIN with the 3rd highest click share.

rank_3_clickshare.description: Click share of the #3 ASIN (0-1 scale).

rank_3_conversionshare.description: Conversion share of the #3 ASIN (0-1 scale).

my_position.description: Your ASIN's position (1, 2, or 3) among top clicked ASINs, or null if not in top 3.

is_weak_leader.description: True if the #1 ASIN has conversion share below the weak_leader threshold (default 15%). Signals displacement opportunity.

leader_conversion_share.description: Conversion share of the #1 ASIN. Lower values = weaker leader = easier to displace.

displacement_opportunity_score.description: Composite score (0-100) combining search volume, leader weakness, and your gap to leader. Higher = better opportunity.

click_share_to_leader.description: Gap between your click share and the leader's. Negative = you trail. Null if you are the leader or not in top 3.

intent_id.description: Grouped mode only (group_by includes 'intent'): the intent bucket identifier (e.g., 'beginner_kit_shopping'), or '__UNCLASSIFIED__' for unclassified terms.

intent_ids.description: All distinct intent_id slugs mapped to this search_term for the row's company.

primary_intent_id.description: Highest-confidence intent_id slug for this search_term.

classification_as_of.description: Date etl.asin_revenue_class_daily was rebuilt for the row that supplied revenue_abcd_class / pareto_abc_class / revenue_share. The classification reflects the trailing 30 days as of THIS date, not the reporting week. The table is rebuilt daily at 07:00 UTC, so treat classes as stale if this date is not today or yesterday.

primary_intent_label.description: Human-readable label of the primary intent. In grouped mode (group_by includes 'intent'), this is the label for the intent_id bucket.

data_freshness.description: Most recent reporting date in the returned data.

warnings.description: Any data quality or coverage warnings.

examples.description: Search terms where my click share is growing — find momentum winners
Defensive alert: search terms where my click share is declining on A-class products
Weak leader opportunities: high-volume keywords where #1 has low conversion share
Track click share trends for specific keywords over 12 weeks
Find search terms where a specific competitor ASIN is in top 3, sorted by search volume
High-volume keywords in a product family where I have some click share but trail the leader
